content.value_statement: Inconsistent tokens and components make Tailwind interfaces difficult to maintain. This skill provides reusable patterns for themes, variants, responsive layouts, forms, and accessibility.
actual_capabilities: Defines semantic color tokens with CSS variables for light and dark themes.
Creates typed React component variants with Class Variance Authority.
Structures compound components for consistent composition and styling.
Builds accessible form controls with labels, error messages, and focus states.
Provides responsive grid and container patterns with explicit variants.
Implements theme persistence, system preference detection, and a theme toggle.
limitations: Examples assume React, TypeScript, and a Tailwind configuration compatible with the documented syntax.
Referenced packages must be installed and configured in the target project.
Generated components still require project-specific accessibility, browser, and visual testing.
The playbook does not provide automated migration or dependency installation.

use_cases.title: Create a component foundation
use_cases.description: Define semantic tokens and reusable component variants for a new React application.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers starting a Tailwind project

use_cases.title: Standardize an existing interface
use_cases.description: Replace inconsistent utility combinations with shared buttons, cards, forms, grids, and theme patterns.

use_cases.title: Improve accessible theming
use_cases.description: Add focus states, form feedback, dark mode, and system theme detection to a product interface.

prompt_templates.title: Define design tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Create semantic Tailwind color and radius tokens for my React project. Include light and dark CSS variables.

prompt_templates.title: Build a component variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed Tailwind button with default, destructive, outline, and icon variants. Include accessible focus and disabled states.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize existing components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these React components and propose shared tokens, CVA variants, and compound component boundaries. Preserve current behavior and identify accessibility gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a complete system
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Tailwind system for this application. Cover tokens, responsive layouts, component variants, forms, dark mode, accessibility, testing, and migration steps.

output_examples.input: Create color tokens for light and dark themes.
output_examples.output: A semantic token plan covering background, foreground, primary, muted, destructive, border, and focus-ring roles for both themes.
A typed button specification with visual variants, size variants, default values, focus behavior, disabled behavior, and composition guidance.
An accessibility review covering labels, input identifiers, validation messages, ARIA relationships, keyboard focus, and recommended verification steps.

best_practices: Use semantic CSS variables so components remain independent from specific palette values.
Compose typed variants and forward references to support consistent reuse.
Test keyboard focus, validation feedback, responsive layouts, and every supported theme.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode palette values inside reusable components.
Do not rely on arbitrary utility values when stable theme tokens are appropriate.
Do not ship components without focus states or accessible names.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: The examples primarily target React and TypeScript projects using Tailwind CSS.

faq.question: Does it support dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents CSS variable themes, system preference detection, local persistence, and a theme toggle.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. You must install and configure Tailwind, CVA, Radix, Lucide, and other selected packages.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing component library?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify shared tokens, variants, composition patterns, and accessibility improvements for existing React components.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides accessible patterns, but the finished interface still requires keyboard, screen reader, contrast, and browser testing.

faq.question: Can it migrate a project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can propose migration steps and component changes, but implementation and validation remain project-specific.
